name: PaymentReturn
label: Payment Return
summary: Sends a settled payment back. A return is a new payment in the opposite direction — it does not undo the original, which stays settled on everyone's books.
whenUsed: Used once a payment has already settled and cannot simply be rejected. Typical triggers: the beneficiary account turns out to be closed, the creditor refuses the funds, or the creditor agent is complying with a camt.056 recall request. Before settlement you reject with pacs.002 instead; that is cheaper and leaves no accounting trail.
gotchas: Returning is not cancelling. The original pacs.008 remains settled and reported; the return is a second, separate settlement. Any system that models a return as deleting the original will not reconcile.

The returned amount is frequently smaller than the original, because agents may deduct their charges from it. ChrgsInf records what was taken, and the difference between OrgnlIntrBkSttlmAmt and RtrdIntrBkSttlmAmt is exactly those charges.
Return Chain records the parties of the return itself, with debtor and creditor swapped relative to the original. Reading it as though it mirrored the original's layout gets the direction backwards.

fields.name: Settlement Information
fields.note: How the return settles. Need not match how the original settled.

fields.name: Return Identification
fields.note: The return's own reference, assigned by the returning agent.

fields.name: Original End To End Identification
fields.note: Preserved so the original debtor can recognise which of its payments came back.

fields.name: Original UETR
fields.note: Links the return to the original in tracking systems. The return itself may also carry its own new UETR.

fields.name: Original Interbank Settlement Amount
fields.note: What settled originally. Compare against the returned amount to see what was deducted.

fields.name: Returned Interbank Settlement Amount
fields.note: What is actually coming back. Mandatory. Often less than the original.

fields.name: Interbank Settlement Date
fields.note: Value date of the return, not of the original.

fields.name: Exchange Rate
fields.note: Where the return crosses currencies, the rate applied — which will rarely be the original rate, so the debtor can end up short through no fault of anyone's.

fields.name: Compensation Amount
fields.note: Interest compensation for the value lost while the funds were misdirected.

fields.name: Charges Information
fields.note: Each agent's deduction from the returned amount, itemised.

fields.name: Return Chain
fields.note: The parties of the return. Debtor and creditor are swapped relative to the original — the original creditor is now returning funds.

fields.name: Return Debtor
fields.note: The party sending the money back, i.e. the original creditor.

fields.name: Return Creditor
fields.note: The party receiving it back, i.e. the original debtor.

fields.name: Return Reason Information
fields.note: Why it is coming back. Repeating.

fields.name: Originator
fields.note: Who decided to return — the creditor, the creditor agent, or an intermediary.

fields.name: Return Reason Code
fields.note: FOCR specifically means 'because you asked us to' — the correct answer to a successful camt.056.

fields.name: Original Transaction Reference
fields.note: Copy of the original payment's details, for matching.

sample: <AddtlInf>Account closed, funds returned less handling fee</AddtlInf>
